findings.title: Programmable static preview metadata is parsed as output tokens on macOS
findings.root_cause: macos/modules/keymap/llm_bridge.lua:413 provider_plain unconditionally parses every provider string through tokens_from_repl and plain_text; :850 uses this result for static programmable preview descriptors although user_code.lua projects row.preview unchanged and callback output uses literal emit_text.
findings.silent_failure: No error; callback still works but braces/key-looking fragments disappear or change in its advertised static description.
findings.regression_test: Run actual programmable preview containing literal {Left} and {U+0041} through real bridge row builder and assert byte-exact descriptor display; retain callback-not-run-on-preview and literal-output controls plus ordinary static TOML output-token preview tests.
original_guarantees: Static programmable preview descriptors are displayed as declared text without evaluating callback output grammar.
Literal callback output and static descriptor metadata do not acquire different token parsing by accident.

findings.title: Catalogue layer_on/layer_off actions do not synchronize the macOS navigation wheel owner
findings.root_cause: macos/modules/gestures/actions.lua:966-972 writes layer_active through ke_variables.set without completion/state publication; macos/modules/shortcuts/actions/system.lua:1048 tracks layer_held only from F20/F19 generator sentinels. CLI variable writes produce no sentinel.
findings.silent_failure: The action and native variable write can succeed without any error while wheel behavior disagrees with the keyboard navigation layer.
findings.regression_test: Compose real action registry and wheel owner; assert entry from layer_on and exit from layer_off after exact-generation successful write, plus refused and superseded writes. Existing probe-gesture-wheel.lua supplies both failing behaviors and a healthy sentinel control.
original_guarantees: The navigation layer wheel and keyboard bindings follow the same accepted activation/deactivation action.
A successful layer_off must not leave wheel events consumed by the layer.

findings.title: Sequential local streams and retries share a request-scoped cumulative thinking filter
findings.reproduction:
{
  "kind": "executed_real_production_composition",
  "artifact": "docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-04-deep/macos-llm/repro-sequential-stream-filter.lua",
  "logs": [
    "docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-04-deep/macos-llm/repro-sequential-stream-filter.log",
    "docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-04-deep/macos-llm/repro-sequential-stream-retry.log",
    "docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-04-deep/macos-llm/repro-sequential-stream-control.log"
  ],
  "steps": [
    "Enable streaming and streaming-multi; choose non-batch profile and two candidates on MLX or Ollama",
    "First independent transport streams its completion and succeeds",
    "Second independent transport streams a different completion; handler treats new prefix as malformed and suppresses interim output until final"
  ],
  "executed": true,
  "runtime": "Lua 5.4.8 + repository Hammerspoon and transport doubles; no native Mac claim"
}
findings.silent_failure: Later token previews stop rendering but final candidates still succeed; only a cumulative-prefix warning identifies the mismatch. Failed partial plus retry has the same outcome.
findings.regression_test: Compose actual local strategy and handler for two successful independent streams and partial-failure/retry. Assert interim rendering for admitted streams and final candidates. Retain valid cumulative and malformed same-stream prefix controls, plus thinking-tag suppression.
original_guarantees: Streaming multi display accepts valid cumulative snapshots from every independent local variant
Thinking filter prefix validation must be scoped to one actual stream, not an entire multi-stream generation

findings.title: Metrics collection pause still records window activity and later credits paused pointer travel
findings.reproduction: Run probe.lua. With collection_suspended=true, real context_tracker appends PAUSED SECRET window_switch and real watcher appends space_change; a 1000px movement during the pause is included by exact snapshot function after resume. Exact real append_log/FIFO body forwards paused title to Rotation.
findings.root_cause: User pause is checked in privacy_context.allows_logging, but watcher/context_tracker production callbacks receive _is_paused that checks global script_control only. LogManager.append_log and Rotation do not apply admission; pointer baseline/state are not reset across user pause.
findings.silent_failure: UI reports collection suspended while identifying activity metadata continues down JSONL/SQL path and paused pointer distance backfills next typing entry. Existing tests gate global pause or typing-only paths.
findings.regression_test: Invoke real Metrics suspend/resume and browser title/app/spaces/mouse callbacks with shared CoreState; assert no paused metadata or pointer delta, allowing previously admitted closing rows.

findings.title: macOS measured passive sleep and lock durations remain zero in dashboard aggregates
findings.reproduction: Run probe.lua. Actual caffeinate callback emits a 60000ms sleep and 30000ms lock passive_period; actual aggregator produces sleep_ms=0, locked_ms=0, passive_count=2.
findings.root_cause: Watchers put durations on passive_period(kind,duration_ms), while aggregator.events only counts that action and credits sleep/lock duration from bare wake/unlock edges. macOS has no Windows-style SQL system-duration rebuild.
findings.silent_failure: Nonzero passive counts accompany zero durations in system manifest and dashboards. Cache replay and foreign imports use same incorrect walker.
findings.regression_test: Replay actual producer event pairs through raw storage/rebuild and aggregate flush/manifest; assert exact lock/sleep durations and no double counting legacy duration-bearing edges.

findings.title: macOS keep-awake completion events never populate keep-awake accounting
findings.reproduction: Run probe.lua. Feed exact producer pair passive_period(kind=awake,duration_ms=120000) and awake_focus(app=Editor,duration_ms=120000) into actual event walker; system awake_ms stays 0.
findings.root_cause: Keep-awake shortcuts emit both accounting records, but macOS aggregator has no duration branch for awake passive periods or app awake_focus. It initializes awake_ms to zero and never increments it.
findings.silent_failure: Dashboard keep-awake totals remain empty and app focus accounting cannot exclude these sessions as UI expects; replay repeats omission.
findings.regression_test: Exercise actual keep-awake stop and auto-stop into live/replay system and app aggregates; verify full interval once globally and expected per-app focus subtraction/toggle.

findings.title: macOS nested lock and sleep transitions overwrite passive interval ownership
findings.reproduction: Run probe.lua. At one-second increments drive lock -> screensDidSleep -> systemWillSleep -> systemDidWake -> screensDidWake -> unlock. Actual watcher emits only one passive_period, kind sleep, duration_ms 1000; lock and earlier sleep segments disappear. Native ordering not measured, sequence uses accepted public callback inputs.
findings.root_cause: Single passive_started_at/passive_kind slot is blindly replaced on every lock/display/system sleep, then cleared by first wake; no independent locked/sleeping state or duplicate-edge idempotence.
findings.silent_failure: Missing durations are absent from raw metrics and unrecoverable by correcting aggregation. Completed count and sleep-vs-lock partition also become inaccurate.
findings.regression_test: Replay nested/repeated lock/sleep/display edges and assert exact non-overlapping partition, pre/post-sleep locked portions, duplicate-edge idempotence and pause/shutdown interval ownership.

findings.title: Failed onboarding Finish retains new configuration locator and locale
findings.reproduction:
{
  "kind": "executed_real_finish_controller",
  "artifact": "docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-04-deep/macos-lifecycle/repro-onboarding-partial-state.lua",
  "log": "docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-04-deep/macos-lifecycle/repro-onboarding-partial-state.log",
  "executed": true,
  "cases": [
    "successful moved-directory control",
    "final writer false",
    "final writer throws",
    "actual destination schema_version=999 refusal before any config batch write"
  ],
  "observed": "Failure closes wizard with error and no reload, while path_writes=1 still names new directory and locale_persists=1."
}
findings.root_cause:
{
  "producer": "macos/ui/onboarding/init.lua:722",
  "later_failure": "macos/ui/onboarding/init.lua:753",
  "failure_handler": "macos/ui/onboarding/init.lua:570",
  "canonical_locator": "macos/infra/config_paths.lua:729",
  "description": "Locator/locale commit before destination versioning and main configuration publication; outer Finish owner has no inverse for these fields."
}
findings.silent_failure: Error claims failed Finish, but locator/locale changes persist independently; later saves resolve new directory while old runtime survives. Original directory is not claimed deleted.
findings.regression_test: Move directory then reject destination schema or fail/throw main publication; require old directory/locale or retained exact compensation debt; retain success and concurrent-external-change controls.
original_guarantees: Failed setup must not silently leave only part of the accepted configuration move published
Configuration locator and destination publication must share exact compensation ownership

findings.title: Restored configuration UI promises restart despite refused or throwing reload
findings.reproduction:
{
  "kind": "executed_real_versions_bridge",
  "artifact": "docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-04-deep/macos-lifecycle/repro-restore-reload-ack.lua",
  "log": "docs/audits/platform-parity/2026-11-04-deep/macos-lifecycle/repro-restore-reload-ack.log",
  "executed": true,
  "cases": [
    "reload true",
    "reload false",
    "reload throws"
  ],
  "observed": "All cases publish restoring,restored; false/throw only log, canonical UI text says app restarts."
}
findings.silent_failure: Disk restore succeeded but old process may remain; page hides restore button and promises restart without exposing reload failure. Linux counterpart shares behavior; Windows reports refusal.
findings.regression_test: Drive restore success with reload true/false/throw and asynchronous abort. Require explicit disk-restored/reload-required state on refusal, backup path retained, and no false restart message.
original_guarantees: Restore success message promising restart must reflect accepted reload ownership
A rejected handoff must not be indistinguishable from successful application of restored settings

findings.title: System-gesture preference probes never start their prepared ShellRunner tasks
findings.root_cause: macos/modules/gestures/conflicts.lua:259-296 calls ShellRunner.spawn and retains/checks handles but never calls handle.start. Real shell_runner.lua:784 prepares, :793 exposes start, :831 returns without starting. snapshot_ready never changes, so conflict slots initially return free.
findings.silent_failure: Refresh returns true without a start error; pending probe never drains and native conflict warning/disable policy has no actual settings snapshot.
findings.regression_test: Use real ShellRunner with recording native task construction/start/terminal; require four starts and terminal/failure settlement; repeat refresh and settings changes, exact shutdown, and fail-closed slot admission before first snapshot. Existing spawn doubles must model prepared/start lifecycle.
original_guarantees: System-owned macOS gesture slots are withheld to prevent native and Ergopti double actions.
An accepted asynchronous preference refresh eventually observes a native terminal or reports failure.

findings.title: Tap commit dispatch bypasses the macOS system-gesture conflict gate
findings.root_cause: engine.lua:700-716 calls dispatchAction directly in tap branch; triggerAction:451-459 alone applies state.system_held. multiFingerAllowed:300 checks physical recognition policy, not native ownership. conflicts.lua:120-127 explicitly declares tap_3 blocking.
findings.silent_failure: Tap logs TAP FIRE with no conflict rejection even when system-held state is true; fixes to preference probing do not fix this independent dispatch omission.
findings.regression_test: Replay real tap commit for taken/unverified/free tap_3 state; assert no dispatch while held and one single-shot dispatch when free, alongside existing swipe control, AI and pause gates.
original_guarantees: A macOS-owned tap_3 slot does not execute an Ergopti action while native Look up owns it.
Tap and swipe dispatch apply the same native-system slot admission.
